ledger.x: 1078: Malik-Shah's brother Tutush takes over Damascus.
1080: Tutush takes Manbij, Hisn al-Faya, Biza'a and Azaz to isolate Aleppo (three-month siege of the city began in 1077).
ledger.cp: holder not named by the page

ledger.x: Undated, placed at 1086: Tutush 'annexed Sidon, Gibelacar, Tiberias, Ramla, Jaffa, and Jerusalem, granting the latter territories to Artuk Bey'; the Artuqids page has Artuk made governor of Jerusalem in 1086 ('Tutush appointed Artuk governor of Jerusalem in 1086').
ledger.cp: holder not named by the page

ledger.x: 1086: Tutush occupies Aleppo 'except for the citadel in May 1086' and leaves in October when Malik-Shah's armies advance; in December Malik-Shah arrives at Aleppo and appoints Aq Sunqur governor.
ledger.cp: holder of Aleppo (not named by the page)

ledger.x: 1086: Tutush leaves Aleppo in October as Malik-Shah's armies advance.
ledger.cp: holder of Aleppo (not named by the page)

ledger.x: 1086: the 1080 belt round Aleppo goes with Aleppo: Malik-Shah appointed Aq Sunqur governor of Aleppo in December 1086; the page does not say what happened to Manbij, Azaz and the other places.
1092: after Malik-Shah's death Tutush takes control of Syria, names himself sultan and in 1092-1093 captures 'Nisbis, Amida, Mayyafariqin and Mosul' in Upper Mesopotamia; the page names no holders.
ledger.cp: holders not named by the page

ledger.x: 1093: Tutush returns to Syria in December 1093.
ledger.cp: holders not named by the page

ledger.x: 1095: Tutush is killed near Ray on 25 February; Ridwan 'took over the Syrian Seljuk throne' at Aleppo and Duqaq 'fled to Damascus, splitting the Syrian Seljuk state'.
1098: the Fatimid vizier al-Afdal Shahanshah expels Sökmen and Ilghazi, the Artuqid governors, from Jerusalem.
1104: Duqaq dies on 6 June and Damascus passes to Toghtekin and the Burids.
1117: Ilghazi takes Aleppo after the assassination of the regent Lu'lu', ending Seljuk rule.
1117: the last Seljuk seat, Aleppo, goes to the Artuqids.

wars.name: Tutush against Aleppo
wars.outcome: Three-month siege of Aleppo in 1077; Manbij, Hisn al-Faya, Biza'a and Azaz taken in 1080; Aleppo occupied except the citadel in May 1086 and left in October when Malik-Shah advanced.

wars.name: Battle of Ain Salm
wars.outcome: Tutush defeated Suleiman ibn Qutulmish, who was killed (his son Kilic Arslan captured); no border change recorded.

wars.name: Tutush in Upper Mesopotamia
wars.outcome: Tutush captured Nisibin, Amida, Mayyafariqin and Mosul in 1092-1093 and returned to Syria in December 1093.

wars.name: Battle of Tell Sultan
wars.outcome: Tutush defeated Aq Sunqur and Bozan in June-July 1094 and took Aleppo.

wars.name: War between Ridwan and Duqaq
wars.outcome: Ridwan defeated Duqaq at Qinnasrin on 22 March 1097; the two lines stayed apart (Ridwan page).

wars.name: Ridwan against the Crusaders and Antioch
wars.outcome: Ridwan lost to Bohemond (5 July 1100) and Tancred (Artah, 20 April 1105), gained and lost Apamea (1106), paid tribute to Tancred and, in 1108, ceded two fortresses near Aleppo (Ridwan page).

certainty.note: City emirates (Damascus, Aleppo) and discs round named towns; no frontier on any page opened.
